Back when Condoleeza Rice joined Dropbox, I got a NAS (Network Attached Storage), which is basically a small low powered server.

Until now it replaces:

  • Dropbox/Google Drive
  • Contact syncing for my Android
  • Calendar syncing for all devices
  • Evernote/Google Keep
  • Google Photo
  • Google Music (to some extent)

It's not complete independence, but it's better than nothing.
Get a NAS to gain some independence from Google
What software are you using to handle the contact and calendar syncing? I run a file server already, but wasn't aware of a solution for those.
CardDAV for contacts and CalDAV (part of WebDAV) for calendar syncing. Those are packages for DiskStation, which is the OS for Synology's NAS.

Yes, I've got one of those. The software is quite amazing. It has saved me untold hours of rummaging around in config files, which would surely be necessary if I had built my own NAS.

Downside is that I can't easily upgrade storage, since the thing has only two HDD bays.

Just built my own recently using freeNAS. The biggest downside is upload speed when you are outside of your LAN. Google drive is still a pretty solid solution due to the amount and distribution of data centers, provided you are encrypting your data before xfering it.

Yeah if you don't have a half decent internet connection, it's not an attractive option.

How was the configuring of freeNAS?

With the latest version of freeNAS it is really straight forward to perform a basic install (no command line required). It will require some Linux knowledge to setup SSL.

My internet connection is on the higher end, but it is hard to compete with any company which has geographically dispersed storage. The main bottleneck I was encountering was xfering a couple GB when out of country.
